standard_prerequisites.name: Simplicial resolution of modules
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the exact complex ... -> g_{n!}(a_n^*G) -> ... -> a^*G -> 0 that Hom(-, F) is applied to.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 2358-2372): for an O-module F on C_total there is a canonical complex 0 -> a_*F -> a_{0,*}F_0 -> a_{1,*}F_1 -> ... of O_D-modules, exact in degrees -1 and 0; if F is injective the complex is exact everywhere and stays exact after applying Hom_{O_D}(G, -) for any O_D-module G.

Yoneda construction (proof lines 2374-2384): by the Yoneda lemma it suffices to construct, functorially in each O_D-module G, the complex of Hom groups; this is done by applying Hom_O(-, F) to the exact simplicial resolution of a^*G (the in-source resolution lemma) and using adjointness of pullback and pushforward.

Exactness (lines 2386-2392): exactness in degrees -1, 0 follows from the construction since Hom_O(-, F) is left exact; if F is injective, Hom_O(-, F) is exact, so the complex is exact in all degrees, and this exactness is preserved by the functor Hom_{O_D}(G, -).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to constructing the complex of Hom groups functorially in G (Yoneda).
Apply Hom_O(-, F) to the simplicial resolution and use adjointness.
Read off exactness from left-exactness, and from exactness of Hom(-, F) in the injective case.
difficulty_reason: Cech-complex lemma (statement 2358-2372, proof 2374-2392): the augmented Cech complex of a module - the proof executes the Yoneda reduction, builds the complex by applying Hom_O(-, F) to the in-source simplicial resolution with adjointness, and derives both exactness statements from exactness properties of Hom; complete as stated. H2.
